title: Supabase Review Quiz
description: Review the small examples from this Supabase course. Take your time and read the reason given for each answer.

questions.question: What protects allowed row access?
options: Hiding a public key in JavaScript
questions.explanation: Supabase stores table data in PostgreSQL and exposes APIs around it. A browser client asks those APIs for allowed data.

questions.question: Which field is the primary key?
questions.explanation: A PostgreSQL table defines the fields used by the API. A primary key gives each record a stable id.

questions.question: Why use known seed records?
options: Their expected query answers are easy to verify
They make all security rules unnecessary
questions.explanation: Seed data is a small set of known records used for learning or testing. It makes query results easy to check.

questions.question: What is needed after enabling RLS for a public read?
questions.explanation: Row-level security adds a database check for rows accessed through client roles. With it enabled and no suitable policy, ordinary client access is denied.

questions.question: Does this SELECT policy permit browser updates?
questions.explanation: A SELECT policy can make fictional sample rows readable to the anon role. Separate SQL privileges and RLS both matter.

questions.question: Which key belongs in this browser sample?
questions.explanation: createClient connects the JavaScript SDK to the chosen project API. Use the local project URL and its public client key for this exercise.

questions.question: What does select("id,title") ask for?
options: Only the id and title columns
questions.explanation: A select request can ask only for the columns a page needs. The client returns data and a possible error.

questions.question: What does gte("pages",50) mean?
questions.explanation: The client can add a filter to a query. gte means greater than or equal to.

questions.question: Why order before limiting?
options: To define which two rows are chosen
questions.explanation: Ordering and limiting help a page request a small useful set. The ordering rule decides which rows are first.

questions.question: What does head:true avoid returning?
questions.explanation: A select can request a count while leaving the row body out. This helps when the page only needs the total.

questions.question: What is the expected result of this browser insert?
questions.explanation: A read-only policy should reject browser writes. Testing the denied path confirms that the page cannot change public records accidentally.

questions.question: Can a frontend environment variable safely contain a service secret?
options: Yes, its variable name hides it
No, bundled values can be read by users
questions.explanation: Local and hosted projects have different addresses and keys. A clear environment setup prevents practice code from changing real data.
